A grep for check-ignore across scripts/ and tests/ returns zero hits; it lives only in .agent-work/ job files (g0-implementer-plan.json:394 and :415, still uncorrected there -- run bookkeeping, out of review scope but worth the Commander knowing it was never fixed at its source). FOUND, same family: scripts/code_map/render.py:397-419 increments npages once per write() CALL, not once per distinct output path, so render_report.json's 'pages' is identical in the healthy world and in a world where pages overwrite each other. r4d-guard-coverage.imperative: Check whether the four ScriptsPackageBundlingTests guards enumerate from the filesystem or from a hand-kept list, and what they are blind to.

The guards enumerate the RIGHT side: ScriptsPackageBundlingTests._source_dirs (tests/test_install_constellation.py:1535-1539) lists directories from the filesystem, not from a hand-kept roster, so a NEW package added under scripts/ goes red until somebody declares it -- I proved the direction by emptying NON_INSTALLABLE_PACKAGES and watching 3 of the 4 guards go red, including test_a_non_installable_package_is_a_package_and_a_flattened_dir_is_not, which is the one that fires on an undeclared package. Two guards also carry explicit non-empty-input preconditions (tests:1547 and tests:1576), so neither can pass vacuously. BLIND SPOT (observation, not a blocker): _source_dirs uses SCRIPTS.iterdir() plus d.glob('*.py'), both non-recursive, so it only sees dirs one level under scripts/ that hold .py files DIRECTLY. A nested package (scripts/code_map/sub/) or a dir whose modules all live one level further down is invisible to all four guards. Second, smaller: test_no_skill_bundles_a_module_from_a_non_installable_package compares BASENAMES, so a future flat scripts/render.py or scripts/extract.py legitimately bundled by a skill would trip it as a false red.

ScriptsPackageBundlingTests is blind below one directory level. _source_dirs (tests/test_install_constellation.py:1535-1539) uses a non-recursive iterdir plus a non-recursive glob('*.py'), so a nested package under scripts/ -- or a directory whose modules sit one level further down -- is invisible to all four guards. The guards are otherwise correctly enumerated from the filesystem. Small fix, worth doing before a second package lands.

Dead state carried from the prototype: extract.Extractor.__init__ takes 'core' and stores self.core (scripts/code_map/extract.py:256-262); nothing reads it and the only construction site (extract.py:766) passes the literal True. Also scripts/code_map/__init__.py:21 points readers at 'NON_INSTALLABLE_SCRIPT_PACKAGES', but the symbol is NON_INSTALLABLE_PACKAGES (scripts/install_constellation.py:135) -- that comment is the only link between the package and its install-side declaration.

The three run-report filenames and the two store filenames live as module constants (extract.STATEMENTS_NAME/REPORT_NAME, supplement.SUPPLEMENT_NAME/REPORT_NAME, render.REPORT_NAME) and are repeated as hand-typed literals in .gitignore:29,30,34,35,36. The narrow one-per-line ignore policy is right; the problem is that nothing ties the lines to the constants, so a renamed store silently starts being committed. A test that asserts each constant's path is ignored would close it, and would itself be falsifiable.

The 'check' subcommand has no execution coverage. tests/test_code_map.py only PARSES 'check' as a subcommand name; nothing calls cli.main(['check', ...]), so all 211 lines of scripts/code_map/checks.py could raise on import or at run time and the suite would stay green. I ran it by hand and it works (exit 0, full diagnostics), but that is my hands, not CI. g1 rewrites this module into real checks, so the cheapest fix is a single smoke test now rather than waiting.
